questions.q: What happens to a relationship built only on romance after about two years?
a: It deteriorates as reality sets in and effort is needed
It settles into an effortless and stable routine
It grows stronger as infatuation deepens
It ends because the couple runs out of conversation
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the early rush fades and couples must then meet each other's needs.

questions.q: Which of these is one of Chapman's five love languages?
a: Acts of service
Shared finances
Common hobbies
Physical fitness
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists words of affirmation, quality time, gifts, acts of service and touch.

questions.q: What does the summary say quality time requires?
a: Undivided attention, with electronics set aside
Expensive dates planned well in advance
Long conversations about your future
Simply being in the same room together
questions.why: Lesson 2 stresses that shared space is not enough without real attention.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest discovering your own love language?
a: Notice what you most often ask your partner for
Take an online personality quiz
Ask friends to describe your character
List the gifts you have given others
questions.why: Lesson 3 also suggests revisiting what made you feel loved or unmet as a child.

questions.q: Why do gifts matter as a love language?
a: The act of choosing or making one conveys how you feel
Their price shows how serious the relationship is
They remove the need for spoken affection
They should only arrive on special occasions
questions.why: Lesson 2 says cost is irrelevant; the gesture itself carries the message.
